title: Perfect inverse-limit reconstruction over an adically complete ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal, with $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Given objects $K_n\in D(A/I^n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ in $D(A/I^{n+1})$ inducing isomorphisms $K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n\simeq K_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], suppose $K_1$ is perfect, meaning isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then $K=R\varprojlim_n K_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is perfect and derived $I$-complete in $D(A)$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], and the canonical maps $K\otimes_A^L A/I^n\to K_n$ are isomorphisms compatible with the transitions.

proof.text: Represent $K_1$ by a bounded finite-projective complex $B$. In each degree choose a retraction from a finite free module $F^i$ onto $B^i$, choosing rank zero above the bound. If $f_i:F^i\to B^i$ and $g_i:B^i\to F^i$ satisfy $f_i g_i=1$, define $d_F=g_{i+1}d_B f_i$. The identity $f_i g_i=1$ proves $d_F^2=0$ and makes $B$ a chain retract of the bounded-above finite-free complex $F$. Its image in the derived category is therefore a direct summand of $Q(F)$. Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-summand] to conclude pseudo-coherence of $K_1$. This includes the zero complex without any ordering assumption on its original support endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0658, lemma-perfect, perfect implies pseudo-coherent; finite-free retraction and split distinguished triangle implementation

proof.text: Put $A_n=A/I^n$. The quotient maps are surjective with square-zero kernels, since $2n\geq n+1$. Adic completeness identifies $A$ with their inverse limit, by lifting a compatible family to an adic Cauchy sequence and using separatedness for uniqueness. The canonical restriction-composition isomorphism satisfies the normalization required by [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-inverse-ring-reconstruction], by the source derived-functor factorization formulas. Apply that declaration with the pseudo-coherent initial term from step 1. Retain pseudo-coherence of $K$, all projection-induced reduction isomorphisms, and a record containing the marked bounded-above flat models $P$ of $K$ and $P_1$ of $K_1$, with the ordinary scalar-reduction chain isomorphism $P\otimes_A A_1\simeq P_1$. The source supplies finite-free terms, hence flat terms. The generic output is projected to this small record before specialization to quotient rings; no object is defined by choosing an unspecified witness. The ring-limit, square-zero-kernel and restriction-composition calculations use the existing proved helpers adic_quotient_limit, adic_step_nilpotent and restrictScalarsComp_derived_factors in PseudoCoherentNormalizedAlgebraTower, now public. Their explicit binders require no Noetherian hypothesis; the Noetherian tower theorem itself is not used.

source.place: Tags 0CQF, 0CQG and 09AW; apply pseudo-coherent reconstruction to the square-zero quotient tower

proof.text: Every maximal ideal contains $I$: use the Mathlib theorem IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot implementing [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical]. Its residue module therefore restricts from $A_1$. The bounded-above free models $P$ over $A$ and $P_1$ over $A_1$ are K-flat by the existing source bounded-above flat-complex theorem. The ordinary natural tensor isomorphism [lem-pc-tensor-restrict-extend-module-natural], with symmetry of tensor, identifies the termwise tensor of $P$ by any $A_1$-module with restriction of the termwise tensor of $P_1$ by that module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-source-kflat-tensor-single-model] on both sides and exactness of restriction of scalars to transfer homology vanishing. A bounded finite-projective representative of $K_1$ supplies a uniform interval by [lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude]. Use the interval $[\min(a,b),b]$ so that it is ordered even when the original perfect representative is zero with reversed endpoints. Apply this to every residue module, then transport along the marking $Q(P)\simeq K$.

source.place: Tag 0CQG, lemma-Rlim-perfect-gives-perfect, residue-field argument; existing source FlatModel.lean and ordinary module tensor comparison

proof.text: The reconstruction in step 2 makes $K$ pseudo-coherent; the interval in step 3 is independent of the maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-maximal-fibre-perfect] to $R=A$, $C=K$ and this interval. It gives perfectness of $K$ without imposing any Noetherian, finite-generation-of-$I$, or regularity hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 068V and 0CQG, last sentence of proof

proof.text: After restriction of scalars to $A$, multiplication by $f^n$ is zero on $K_n$ for every $f\in I$: this scalar has zero image in $A/I^n$, and hence acts as the zero endomorphism of every complex representing $K_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-torsion-derived-limit-complete] with $L_n=K_n$ and exponent $e=n$. It proves derived $I$-completeness in the sense of the vanishing definition [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], not merely an identification with the limit of ordinary reductions.

source.place: Tags 091W and 09AV, completeness argument used by 09AW

proof.text: The first two arrows of the specified Roos distinguished triangle compose to zero, so $p(1-s)=0$. Composing with the nth product projection gives $p_{n+1}t_n=p_n$. The unit formula for the adjunction hom-equivalence identifies $p_n$ with the unit followed by restriction of adicLimitReduction at level n. Substitute these equalities to obtain exactly the displayed consecutive-level compatibility. No extra normalization or chain representative is needed for this step.

lean.statement: theorem rlim_perfect_complete {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] [∀ n : ℕ, HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))] (K : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, K (n + 1) ⟶ (adicStepRestriction I n).obj (K n)) (L : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))) (adj : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⊣ adicLevelRestriction I n) (B : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1 + 1))) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))) (badj : ∀ n : ℕ, B n ⊣ adicStepRestriction I n) (hbase : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (((badj n).homEquiv (K (n + 1)) (K n)).symm (t n))) (hperfect : IsPerfect (K 0)) [HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ (adicLevelRestriction I n).obj (K n))] (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (p : C ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (adicLevelRestriction I n).obj (K n))) (δ : ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (adicLevelRestriction I n).obj (K n)) ⟶ C⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (hlim : IsDerivedLimitTriangle (adicTowerTransition I K t) C p δ) : IsPerfect C ∧ IsDerivedComplete I C ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (adicLimitReduction I K L adj C p n)) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (adj (n + 1)).unit.app C ≫ (adicLevelRestriction I (n + 1)).map (adicLimitReduction I K L adj C p (n + 1)) ≫ adicTowerTransition I K t n = (adj n).unit.app C ≫ (adicLevelRestriction I n).map (adicLimitReduction I K L adj C p n)
